accepted.rationale: Verifying a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message, or any certificate chain, with CRL checking enabled spends CPU time that grows with the square of the input: crl_crldp_check() in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c rebuilds the full name of every CRL distribution point of a certificate for every CRL it checks, so a certificate with many distribution points exhausts the verifier's CPU (OpenSSL's fix, pull request 33546). A denial of service only, CWE-400, CVSS 3.1 7.5 from CISA-ADP, NVD's analysis pending; CISA's SSVC record of 2026-11-19 gives exploitation none, and the scan's database records no known exploitation (EPSS 0.00359).
accepted.mitigation: No exposure path was identified in the configuration examined, which is not a guarantee that the flaw cannot be exploited (D-139). Nothing in the image verifies with CRL checking. OpenSSL reaches crl_crldp_check() only from check_revocation(), which returns at once without X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK (openssl-3.5.9 crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c lines 1041 to 1045). PHP 8.5's OpenSSL extension sets no verification flag and loads no CRL into a verification store (php-src PHP-8.5 ext/openssl/openssl.c and xp_ssl.c), so the application's outbound HTTPS through Guzzle's StreamHandler (app/Domain/Operations/OutboundHttp.php) verifies without CRLs. libpq 18 sets the flag only when a root certificate file and a CRL file are both present (src/interfaces/libpq/fe-secure-openssl.c lines 932 to 971); the image configures neither sslrootcert nor sslcrl and holds no ~/.postgresql/root.crt. curl checks CRLs only with --crlfile or CURLOPT_CRLFILE, which nothing sets, and its one use at run time is the health check over plain HTTP on the loopback address. Nginx serves plain HTTP on port 8080, with no ssl_crl and no client certificate, TLS ending before the container; and nothing in app/, config/, bootstrap/, routes/, docker/, compose.yaml or the scripts verifies a CMS or PKCS#7 message.
